fix.redesign: replace with reboilerMMBtuHr, label "Reboiler duty", unit MMBtu/hr, to six decimals, tol 1e-5: step six of the beginner worked lesson (circulation gpd x (sensible + overhead Btu/gal) / 24000000), computed from the reflux ratio 0.22 and the prompt conditions the capstone already states. Alternative: keep BTEX and add the ppmv mole balance as a step in beginner m05 or the worked lesson.

fields.recommendation: Redesign or teach. As posed the beginner tier never teaches the ppmv mole balance (the worked lesson defers it to a later tier), the fc-water-explorer BTEX view is fixed on OBIAFU, and the Suite prints 1 decimal (38.7 against 38.678402, tol 1e-5). The reboiler duty uses the reflux ratio the prompt states but grades nothing.
fields.evidence: 155e-6 x 0.12 x 47e6 / 379.48357 x 92 x 365/2000 = 38.678402 reproduces the key, but none of that chain is in the beginner lessons; the only beginner BTEX mentions are a table column (m05 l05) and the default MW 92 (m01 l02).
fields.notes: The prompt already states a reflux ratio of 0.22 that no graded field uses, which suits the replacement.

rekey_annot.source_ref: src/content/courses/gasprocessing/beginner/m06-the-associate-reading/l02-the-capstone-worked.md (step five and step six); tools/course-waves/gasprocessing/fc4_capstone.mjs (engine tegPackage reboilerMMBtuHr)
rekey_annot.prompt_precision: the duty in MMBtu an hour, to six decimals
rekey_annot.evidence: From the prompt alone: water 47 x (66.845130 - 5) = 2906.7211 lb/day, circulation x 3.6 = 10464.196 gal/day, sensible 9.3 x 0.55 x (368 - 109) = 1324.785 Btu/gal, overhead (1/3.6) x 1100 x 1.22 = 372.7778 Btu/gal, duty 10464.196 x 1697.5628 / 24000000 = 0.740151 MMBtu/hr; reproduces the engine value 0.7401512387317987 exactly. Six decimals round within 5e-7 of tol 1e-5. Neighbours fail: sensible only 0.5776, no reflux 0.7122. The leak guard (panelCapstoneGuard, gasprocessingLab leak gate) finds no teaching number within ten bands; the worked lesson's duty is the teaching case 0.697269.

fields.prompt_precision: Removals as a fraction, stages, circulations in gpm and the duty in MMBtu an hour, to six decimals.
fields.evidence: Kremser (A^(N+1) - A)/(A^(N+1) - 1) at A 1.85, N 5 = 0.97825502; reproduced exactly. Tol 5e-7 equals the half unit at six decimals; the six-decimal rounding here is off by 1.6e-8, so it passes.
fields.notes: Tol sits exactly at half a unit of the stated precision; honest for this value but leaves no float margin.

fields.prompt_precision: Removals as a fraction, stages, circulations in gpm and the duty in MMBtu an hour, to six decimals.
fields.evidence: N = ln((A - E)/(1 - E))/ln A - 1 at E 0.94 = 3.419967; reproduced exactly; tol 1e-6 is twice the half unit.
fields.notes: The Suite sweetening card prints acid gas 0 dp, circulation 0 dp, reboiler 1 dp (SweeteningDewPanels.jsx:73-77) and stages 1 dp (DehydrationPanels.jsx:108); fc-absorber-explorer has no inputs (mode select only, AbsorberExplorer.jsx:332).

fields.evidence: acid moles / 0.31 x 105.14 / 0.33 / 63.635283 x 7.480519 / 1440 = 734.577676 (with the engine's 8.34 lb/gal water base it is 734.5776759, exact). Tol 1e-5 is a relative 1.4e-8.
fields.notes: Tight: the learner must use the lesson-printed DEA solution density (m05 l04) or back 8.34 lb/gal out of MDEA's 64.883034; a textbook water density (62.4 lb/ft3, 8.33 lb/gal) misses by about 0.015 gpm. The 8.34 base itself is printed only in advanced m06 l01.

fields.source_ref: src/components/course/panels/gasprocessing/ColdEndExplorer.jsx:332 (typed mode: the case typed as the prompt states it)
fields.prompt_precision: The derivative per degR, the coefficient in degF a psi, temperatures in degF and water contents in lb a MMscf, all to six decimals.
fields.evidence: A typed skid mode on ColdEndExplorer.jsx (typedColdEnd in gasprocessingLab.js: jouleThomsonFPerPsi, jtDrop at the default 20 steps and saturatedWaterContent, the calls the capstone derivation makes) takes the let-down the learner types. Typing 935 psia, 87 degF, 405 psia, 0.67 and 10.2 prints the value within tol; yourCase.test.jsx proves it, that the AGBADA default lands on no graded answer, and that one retyped input misses. The Suite dew point card stays a backup route (W3).

shipped.prompt: On the course panel, the Cold end explorer's "Your skid, typed" view takes the five numbers above (inlet pressure and temperature, separator pressure, gravity and molar heat capacity) and prints every value to at least the precision graded here.
